title: This Chart Has Predicted Almost Every US Recession. It's Called The Yield Curve.
description:
Educational purposes only. Not financial advice.

Normally, longer-term government bonds pay higher interest than short-term ones, because lending money for longer carries more risk. When that flips — when short-term Treasury yields rise above long-term yields — it's called a yield curve inversion, and it has historically preceded most US recessions. It reflects investors betting the Fed will need to cut rates later because growth is slowing. Educational content only, not financial advice.
